extracted.intended_audience: educated readers and reform-minded public (Liberal intellectuals, politicians, and those interested in cultural criticism)
extracted.subtask_description: An essay-form set of standards and evaluative principles about culture, moral and religious practice, and the proper way to pursue social and political reform; aimed at guiding thought and action rather than providing procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture as Hellenising development
rubrics_metrics.description: The development of our Hellenising instincts, seeking skilfully the intelligible law of things, and making a stream of fresh thought play freely about our stock notions and habits, is what is most wanted by us at present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate the Hellenic impulse to understand underlying principles; encourage flexible, intelligent habits of thought rather than mechanical routines. Use reading, observation, and thinking to approach the intelligible law of things.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture brings one toward right reason (authority of reason)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only in right reason can we get a source of sure authority, and culture brings us towards right reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When public authority is lacking or uncertain, seek justification in cultivated, reasoned judgment rather than in sectarian or mechanical rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for harmonious perfection of humanity (sweetness and light)
rubrics_metrics.description: What we want is a fuller harmonious development of our humanity, a free play of thought upon our routine notions, spontaneity of consciousness, sweetness and light; and these are just what culture generates and fosters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educative practices and reforms should aim at harmonising intellectual, moral, and aesthetic faculties—promoting refinement and humane sensibility rather than mere strength or zeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use books and learning instrumentally, not pedantically
rubrics_metrics.description: Culture has got its name touched ... with a sort of air of bookishness and pedantry ... from the follies of the many bookmen who forget the end in the means, and use their books with no real aim at perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading and scholarship must be pursued with the goal of human improvement; avoid mere display of learning or abstruse generalities disconnected from moral or intellectual development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep close to common fact when lacking systematic philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: An unpretending writer, without a philosophy based on inter-dependent, subordinate, and coherent principles, must not presume to indulge himself too much in generalities, but he must keep close to the level ground of common fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practical argument and public counsel, ground claims in observable facts and ordinary understanding when lacking formal scientific training—avoid speculative abstractions that detach from lived realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer operations based on reason and justice over mechanical maxims
rubrics_metrics.description: The actual power ... by virtue of which the Liberal party ... is not the power of reason and justice, it is the power of the Nonconformists' antipathy to Church establishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or conducting reforms, examine whether motives are founded on reason and justice rather than on stock notions, fetishes, or mechanical rules; prefer measures that can be defended by reasoned argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective reform must win affections and be persuasive
rubrics_metrics.description: An operation performed in virtue of a mechanical rule, or fetish ... does not easily inspire respect in its adversaries, and make their opposition feeble and hardly to be persisted in, as an operation evidently done in virtue of reason and justice might.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design reforms to appeal to the understanding and affections of those affected; persuasion rooted in truth and justice produces durable change, whereas fetish-driven actions provoke counter-fetishes and hostility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bring stock maxims within free thought (Hellenise rather than Hebraise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let our consciousness play freely round the stock notion or habit on which their operation relies ... dissolve these motives if they are unsound ... and create in their stead ... sounder and more persuasive motives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before endorsing or executing a popular maxim or policy, subject it to reflective critique; transform crude rules into reasoned principles that can command assent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret religious precepts by their function (inward persuasion vs outward constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Christ's words mean that his religion is a force of inward persuasion acting on the soul, and not a force of outward constraint acting on the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When citing religious authority for public policy, test whether the interpretation furthers inner moral persuasion and communal good; reject literalist uses that impose external fetishes contrary to religion's inward aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate individual thought and collective worship
rubrics_metrics.description: Thought and speculation is eminently an individual matter, and worship and devotion is eminently a collective matter ... Man worships best, therefore, with the community; he philosophises best alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve private intellectual freedom while recognising the social and public importance of collective religious or civic rituals; public establishments can enhance the emotive and unifying aspects of worship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design worship to be as common and non-divisive as possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Worship ... should be as much as possible a common and public act ... 'The best prayers are those which have nothing distinct about them, and which are thus of the nature of simple adoration.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public religious forms should minimize sectarian distinctiveness to maximize communal devotion and social cohesion; grandeur and publicity in worship can strengthen collective feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base social/political rules on duties revealed by consciousness rather than on abstract rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If he simply and naturally reads his consciousness, discover that he has any rights at all? ... the more it seems to tell me that I have no rights at all, only duties; and that men get this notion of rights from a process of abstract reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and moral judgment should emphasise duties (what consciousness shows us to be ours to do) and be wary of treating abstract 'rights' as absolute justifications without considering concrete duties and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid one-size-fits-all legal fixes; adapt to circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether our children's welfare is best served by their all sharing equally in our property depends on circumstances and on the state of the community in which we live.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal reforms (e.g., intestacy rules) must be evaluated for efficacy in particular social contexts; mechanical equalizing rules may undermine other goods like social stability or child welfare in certain historical circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor gradual cultural persuasion (culture) over abrupt legislative coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: These considerations, when culture has called them forth and given them free course in our minds, will live and work. They will work gradually, no doubt, ... everything teaches us how gradually nature would have all profound changes brought about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use education, reflection, and the slow dissemination of truth and reason to effect change; recognise the long-term efficacy of 'sweetness and light' over immediate forceful interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate perpetuation of classes by their real effects on individual and communal welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the perpetuation of such a class is for its own real welfare and for the real welfare of the community, depends on the actual circumstances of this class and of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess institutions (like hereditary landowning) by empirical and moral effects: do they discipline and serve the common good in present circumstances, or do they foster ease, abuse, and false ideals?

rubrics_metrics.name: Reforms should cultivate delicacy of perception and the 'best self', not mere liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: The Philistine's perfection ... to cultivate in him this delicacy, to render it independent of external and mechanical rule, and a law to itself, is what seems to make most for his perfection, his true humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim at moral and aesthetic education that refines taste and conscience rather than simply expanding unregulated personal liberty; perfect freedom is service and harmonising impulses under a higher ideal of humanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: State religious policy: apportion public religious endowments by large, lasting differences
rubrics_metrics.description: The State is of the religion of all its citizens, without the fanaticism of any of them ... apportion between those several forms, with due regard to circumstances, taking account only of great differences, which are likely to be lasting, and of considerable communions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In dealing with church endowments or disestablishment, the State should aim for fair apportionment among enduring and significant religious communities, avoiding petty divisions and fanatic concessions.
